stories.headline: Youri Tielemans: 'Everything was missing' in Man United's loss to Como
stories.summary: Youri Tielemans admitted "everything was missing" in Manchester United's humiliating defeat to Como.
stories.body:
Youri Tielemans admitted "everything was missing" in Manchester United's humiliating defeat to Como.

Michael Carrick's position is hanging in the balance as a poor start to the season reached a nadir in Wednesday's 4-1 Champions League loss in Italy.

The fact United skipper Bruno Fernandes publicly questioned the head coach's approach increased the speculation over his future ahead of Sunday's return to Premier League action at home to Bournemouth.

Summer signing Tielemans told MUTV: "It wasn't a great atmosphere in [the dressing room], which everyone can understand, but we need to move on.

"We have got games coming, but it was very poor [against Como].

"Everything was missing. We were disjointed as a team, we didn't play well together, our press was off.

"When we were on the ball, we couldn't make the right decisions. Obviously you get frustrated in the game and they played around us too easily so, like I said, it was a poor night."

Furious Carrick marched over to the away section at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia to apologise to the remaining United fans at the final whistle.

Tielemans echoed the manager's sentiments but knows performances are all that matter after United went a seventh straight match without a win.

- Man United's worst league starts ever: How does 2026-27 compare?

- Jamie Carragher slams Bruno Fernandes for Michael Carrick criticism: 'Absolute disgrace'

- Fàbregas, Paz dedicate historic Man United rout to loyal Como fans

"They travel all the way and don't want to see this," the midfielder said.

"The only thing we can do now is apologise. But we can apologise as much as we want, we just need to put the performance out on the pitch and at the moment we aren't doing that.

"It's tough times for them, especially supporting the club, and we have to fight as players."

stories.headline: Christian Horner to Mercedes? Ex-Red Bull boss reveals pre-Toto Wolff approach
stories.summary: Christian Horner has revealed he rejected an offer to become Mercedes' Formula 1 team principal in 2012, before the team appointed his future rival Toto Wolff.
stories.body:
Christian Horner has revealed he rejected an offer to become Mercedes' Formula 1 team principal in 2012, before the team appointed his future rival Toto Wolff.

Horner claims in his new autobiography, Drive, that F1 legend and Mercedes' new non-executive chairman Niki Lauda -- with whom he had previously discussed Lewis Hamilton's future -- visited his home during the off-season and offered him a substantial salary to leave Red Bull.

The former Red Bull boss says he turned down the opportunity out of loyalty to the team he had helped build, with Mercedes subsequently embarking on a period of dominance under Wolff and Hamilton.

"Maybe our interactions over Lewis had stuck with him because later that year, during the Christmas break, Niki came to my house and asked me to join Mercedes as his team principal," Horner wrote.

"I was caught off guard. Leaving Red Bull had never crossed my mind. When he then laid out a series of dazzling numbers, I realized he was discussing my potential salary.

"'Red Bull will never pay you what Mercedes can,' he said. 'I respect you as a racer. I want you to come. Besides, Helmut [Marko, Red Bull adviser] is a miserable b------.'"

The approach came after Horner had held discussions with Lauda about Hamilton's future, with the British driver considering leaving McLaren at the end of the 2012 season. Hamilton held ultimately unfruitful talks with Red Bull due to the finances involved, but Horner knew Lauda and Mercedes would be interested.

Indeed, Hamilton joined Mercedes for 2013, while Horner remained at Red Bull, where Vettel had just secured his third consecutive world championship.

"I listened to his offer and shook my head," Horner wrote. "At that point, Sebastian was at the peak of his powers and Red Bull were in the ascendancy.

"'Niki, I've been winning World Championships with Red Bull,' I said. 'I've built everything from scratch. I feel a loyalty to Dietrich and the team. So as much as I appreciate this, I'm not going to join Mercedes.'"

- Horner: Red Bull blocked moves for Leclerc and Alonso

- Rafael Câmara to Haas: How he could shake up Ferrari's future

- How Kimi Antonelli can win the F1 title at the US Grand Prix

Mercedes subsequently recruited Wolff from Williams in January 2013, with the Austrian going on to oversee one of the most successful periods in F1 history.

Mercedes won eight consecutive constructors' championships between 2014 and 2021, while Hamilton claimed six drivers' titles with the team.

Horner, meanwhile, remained at Red Bull until his dismissal in July 2025, overseeing four world championships with Vettel and another four with Max Verstappen.

Reflecting on Mercedes' decision to bring Hamilton and Wolff together, Horner admitted he initially underestimated the significance of the partnership.

"Their union was interesting but seemingly inconsequential," he wrote.

"In my mind, I was helping a friend while weakening McLaren, who were our closest rivals at that time. So, what was the worst that could happen?"

Drive, Christian Horner's autobiography, will be released on Oct. 22.

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Man United consider defensive clearout in summer
stories.summary: Manchester United are considering refreshing their back four, with three senior defender's contracts up at the end of the season. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Manchester United are considering refreshing their back four, with three senior defender's contracts up at the end of the season. Meanwhile, Arsenal want £55 million in any potential deal for striker Viktor Gyökeres.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Harry Maguire, Luke Shaw, and Lisandro Martínez are playing for their futures at Old Trafford, with their contracts due to expire next summer. That's according to according to TEAMtalk, which claims that United are not rushing to make a decision on the three defenders. That comes as preparations are being put in place for potential defensive reinforcements in 2027, with center back and left back set to be the main areas of consideration.

- Chelsea are showing interest in a move for Brighton midfielder Yasin Ayari, claims TEAMtalk. The 23-year-old Sweden international is in talks with the Seagulls over a contract extension, with his deal expiring in the summer, though the club has the option to extend it by a further year. However, while there are hopes of sealing a long-term stay with the club, talks have stalled over an improved contract. That has brought Chelsea into the conversation, with the Blues eyeing another swoop on Brighton, while Turkish Super Lig side Galatasaray are also monitoring the situation.

- If Viktor Gyökeres does leave Arsenal in the next year, then the North London club has set a valuation of £55 million on a potential exit, reports Football Insider. That is the same amount as the initial fee the Gunners paid Sporting CP to land the striker last summer. However, after a slow start to the current campaign, the Sweden international continues to be linked with a possible move away. Clubs in Italy, Spain, and elsewhere in England are keeping track of the situation, should the 28-year-old become available.

- Arsenal are among a group of teams following a potential switch for Monza striker Gustavo Varela. That's according to Mundo Deportivo, which claims that the Gunners are joined by Napoli and the 21-year-old's former club, Benfica, in keeping track of his progress. Varela has scored eight goals in seven matches across all competitions for Monza, making an impressive start with his new club. While Benfica is keen on a return, there is no clause that could guarantee a move back to Portugal, though there is a clause that will allow for the club to match an offer accepted from another club. However, with Arsenal and Napoli in the mix, that prospect has been described as difficult.

- Liverpool are in no rush to engage in conversations with Alexis Mac Allister over a new contract, despite the player voicing his disappointment at the lack of an offer earlier this season. That's according to The Telegraph, which claims that the Reds are yet to open talks, as the Argentina international has entered the final two years of his deal at Anfield. The 27-year-old moved to Merseyside from Brighton for £35 million back in 2023, and has featured 161 times for Liverpool since then.

Other rumors
- Manchester United, Arsenal and Newcastle United have all been keeping track of AS Roma defender Wesley, with the 23-year-old Brazilian valued between €50 million and €60 million by the Serie A club. (TEAMtalk)

- Nine clubs are tracking a potential move for Eintracht Frankfurt youngster Niko Ilićević, including the likes of Liverpool, Manchester City, Chelsea and Tottenham from England, alongside Barcelona and Real Madrid in Europe. The attacking midfielder has been monitored heavily by several other clubs. (TEAMtalk)

- Manchester City, Chelsea, Newcastle United, Everton and Leeds United are the latest teams to be tracking Club Brugge striker Nicolò Tresoldi, 22, after attracting attention from plenty of teams with his Champions League displays. (Ekrem Konur)

- Barcelona and Atletico Madrid are among the sides monitoring the future of Lisandro Martínez, with the Manchester United defender now in the final year of his contract. United hold the option of an extra year on his deal. (Ekrem Konur)

- Liverpool are continuing to work on a new contract for Rio Ngumoha, with the club setting a clear stance on no exit for the 18-year-old winger in the coming transfer windows. (Fabrizio Romano)

- Lorenzo Lucca could leave Napoli in the January transfer window, with the 26-year-old striker free to move in the winter. (Nicolò Schira)

stories.headline: Angel Reese keeps Dream rolling with Game 3 win over Valkyries in WNBA Finals
stories.summary: Angel Reese kept the Dream rolling in Game 3 with a 97-71 win as Atlanta took a 2-1 lead over the Valkyries in the WNBA Finals.
stories.body:
ATLANTA -- Angel Reese continued to bark at anyone in her vicinity -- the opponent, her teammates, even the officials -- during Wednesday night's Game 3 of the WNBA Finals. At one point, she even took a moment to celebrate with six-time All-Star Alyssa Thomas, who was sitting courtside.

Reese explained her mentality in simple terms after leading the Dream to a 97-71 win over the Golden State Valkyries that put Atlanta two wins away from its first WNBA championship

"Y'all not taking this from us, and that's in my heart," Reese said. "Like, I'm not letting you take this from us. I think [that confidence] becomes contagious within the team. They feel that confidence too."

Reese, a three-time All-Star, has fully evolved into the emotional leader of the Dream, who took a 2-1 lead in the series. In the process, she continued to set league records, as she finished with 21 points and 12 rebounds, making her the youngest player in Finals history to record three straight double-doubles and joining A'ja Wilson as the only players to record 20 points and 10 rebounds in consecutive Finals games.

A sold-out crowd of 17,099 had State Farm Arena rocking as Atlanta finally found its offense after a pair of low-scoring affairs in San Francisco.

"I knew it was coming, especially back home," Reese said of Wednesday's offensive output. "It feels good to be home on your own court and you've seen the basket that you shoot on every single day. ... Everybody contributed from top to bottom.

"And when you shoot 49%, I mean, you win games."

The Dream shot a series-high 49.3% from the field and knocked down nine 3-pointers, their most of these Finals. Rhyne Howard found her flow with 16 points, four assists and four rebounds while becoming the first player in league history to record five steals in consecutive Finals games. Naz Hillmon added 15 points, DeWanna Bonner put up 12 off the bench and Jordin Canada finished with 10 points, six rebounds and eight assists.

It was just the third time in the 2026 playoffs that a team shot better than 45% from the field against the Valkyries.

"We definitely showed that we played a little more free tonight, and we got easier looks because of it," Howard said. "We weren't stressed. We just let the game come to us, and we went out and we won.

"Our attention to detail, our spacing, making sure that we're moving, giving people the lanes to drive the ball, finding each other for open shots. We were more together on that end of the floor and ... we were just feeding off of each other."

The Valkyries continued to turn the ball over at an alarming rate, committing 17 turnovers Wednesday night that the Dream turned into 22 points. Golden State had 18 turnovers in the Game 2 loss.

Points also continued to be hard to come by for Golden State, which shot 34.8% from the floor. Gabby Williams scored a team-high 15, and Cecilia Zandalasini and Janelle Salaun tallied 13 apiece. (That was a playoff high for Salaun after her postseason minutes had been reduced.) Tiffany Hayes kept the team in the game early and finished with 14 points off the bench.

"I think this game, they wanted it more than us, and that's not who we are," Hayes said. "That's not who we've been, and that's not how we got here.

"[The turnovers are] a lot of us being undisciplined. ... Uncharacteristic of us."

Before Wednesday's contest, Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase said there was nothing she liked about Game 2 and was insistent that her team was ready to fight.

"Sometimes, promises aren't kept," she said afterward. "I think there's sometimes individual punches and some people with great spurts and some people with great energy. But it's like, well, then how can we do it all together?

"The will is there, the want to is there, but the fight together, I'm missing -- the piece of putting it together."

stories.headline: St. Louis City beats Columbus in Open Cup final for club's first trophy
stories.summary: St. Louis City won the first trophy in the club's history on Wednesday after defeating Columbus Crew on penalties to lift the U.S. Open Cup.
stories.body:
Backup goalkeeper Ben Lundt made a key save in the penalty shootout of a 120-minute 0-0 tie with the Columbus Crew to help St. Louis City SC win the Lamar Hunt U.S. Open Cup on Wednesday night.

Timo Baumgartl gave St. Louis a 1-0 lead on the first penalty kick and then Lundt dove to his left to get a hand on Santiago Rodriguez's shot that deflected off the post.

St. Louis went 5 for 5 in the shootout, capped by Daniel Edelman's shot down the middle as goalkeeper Nicholas Hagen went the wrong way. Lukas MacNaughton, Chris Durkin and Damion Downs also scored.

St. Louis earned a spot in the 2027 CONCACF Champions Cup after securing the first major trophy in club history.

Columbus was seeking its second U.S. Open Cup title in club history.

Lundt entered the game in the 78th minute after starter Roman Bürki took a knee to the head while making a save. Bürki waved to the crowd while being carted off the field. Lundt came on in relief for his fourth appearance of the season.

It was the first U.S Open Cup final to go to penalties since 2015 when Sporting Kansas City beat the Philadelphia Union. The USOC is open to both professional and amateur clubs, but Major League Soccer teams have dominated the competition for more than two decades.

stories.headline: Dodgers' Shohei Ohtani won't require surgery, expected to pitch in 2027
stories.summary: Shohei Ohtani will not require surgery to treat any ailment he dealt with this past season, Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said Wednesday. And: "I fully expect him to pitch next year," Friedman added.
stories.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Shohei Ohtani will not require surgery to treat his left knee or right arm or any other ailment he dealt with throughout the second half of this past season, Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said Wednesday.

Doctors merely prescribed rest. The expectation is that his 2027 season will be unaffected. When Ohtani begins his preparations for it, he will train as a two-way player.

"I fully expect him to pitch next year," Friedman said during an end-of-season news conference at Dodger Stadium.

But what that looks like has yet to be determined.

"This is unprecedented, what he's doing," Friedman added. "So obviously for us it's unprecedented. We don't have any experience to draw from. We can't go look at how other situations have played out to try to learn from the good and the bad. We have to all just figure it out together. And I'm not only expecting him to pitch; we're excited about him pitching. So now it's about: How do we do that? How do we manage through a long season and have him at his best going into October? That's a challenge."

Ohtani was a diminished version of himself by the time October arrived. He ended the regular season with 11 hits and 29 strikeouts over his last 70 at-bats and went 4-for-22 with no extra-base hits in his first seven postseason games. Ohtani finally broke through with a home run in Game 4 of the National League Championship Series, his first since Aug. 18, but it was too late for a Dodgers team that was ultimately swept by the Milwaukee Brewers.

Asked if the Dodgers could have managed Ohtani's two-way status differently to put him in a better spot for October, Friedman said: "I don't know the answer to that. It's one of those things that -- the injuries started in early July. Through mid-August, he was still I think the consensus MVP."

Ohtani went 8-2 with a 1.79 ERA in his first 14 starts, striking out 95 batters and issuing 26 walks in 85⅔ innings. But continual pain in his left knee and right biceps prevented him from pitching beyond July 3. As of Aug. 18, he was slashing .294/.390/.558 with 30 home runs and seven stolen bases. But physical discomforts started to merge into his at-bats, ultimately throwing his mechanics out of whack. Ohtani was not put on the injured list until after Labor Day, giving him only five regular-season games to get reacclimated to major league pitching before the playoffs.

Speaking after the Dodgers' season-ending 6-4 loss on Oct. 15, Ohtani said he was "not quite satisfied with how things shaped up on the pitching side."

"I haven't been able to really come to grips with what I've learned overall this season," Ohtani added through an interpreter. "It's something that I'm going to go back to the drawing board in terms of treatment, training programs and see what I can come up with for next season."

Ohtani was attempting his first full-time two-way season in three years, and doing so at age 32 proved more difficult than at 29. Friedman acknowledged that Ohtani's offensive struggles "certainly had an impact" on the Dodgers' early exit. But the entire offense slumped, combining to post a .590 OPS in the postseason and go 4-for-27 with runners in scoring position in the NLCS.

Friedman announced there would be no changes to Dave Roberts' coaching staff and said it was "business as usual" with owner Mark Walter, who is under federal investigation over alleged multibillion-dollar self-dealing.

"We talked to Mark after we lost," Friedman said, "and he was obviously really disappointed. But so much of his focus was on, 'OK, what can we do? What are our plans?'"

The Dodgers' brain trust hasn't necessarily figured that out just yet.

At the forefront of their minds will be the pending free agency of Tarik Skubal, the ace pitcher they acquired before the trade deadline, as well as several important relievers, most notably Alex Vesia and Evan Phillips.

The team also announced Wednesday that catcher Dalton Rushing and right-hander Will Klein both underwent elbow procedures; Rushing will be sidelined approximately nine months after an internal brace procedure, while Klein will be ready for spring training after having a bone chip removal and spur cleanup.

Meanwhile, Friedman and his group will be trying to figure out how to inject some youth into baseball's oldest position player group. But nothing will be more important than their plan with Ohtani -- specifically how they handle his pitching so that he makes an impact on the mound without it affecting his offense.

The Dodgers could opt to start his season as a pitcher later, or work in more off days in between, or perhaps some combination of both. For this to work, several people within the organization believe, Ohtani will have to be more forthcoming with his ailments. One question the Dodgers haven't seemingly figured out is how much autonomy Ohtani will have over how this plays out.

One thing seems certain: Friedman, and perhaps the Dodgers as a whole, value his pitching enough to give it another try.

"I think we're just going to have to be very deliberate about it on all sides," Friedman said of the back-and-forth communication, "because the value of it is incredible, and therefore it's incumbent upon all of us to figure out the best way to do it."

stories.headline: Retirement doesn't scare Alexander Volkanovski, but neither does fighting at 40
stories.summary: Even at 38 years old, UFC featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski says he will deliver one of the finest performances of his career at UFC 333.
stories.body:
Retirement, for all professional athletes no matter their craft, is inevitable.

But as the next phase of Alexander Volkanovski's life peeks up from beyond the horizon, the UFC featherweight champion says he will deliver a performance at UFC 333 that leaves MMA fans in awe.

"You guys will come out of this being like that's one of Volk's best performances. That's the best way for me to put it," Volkanovski told ESPN after wrapping up a session at the new home of Freestyle MMA.

The gym, which is around 10 times the size of coach Joe Lopez's former premises, is a symbol of the duo's amazing journey from relative MMA obscurity to, at one point, the top of the UFC pound-for-pound rankings.

Volkanovski now sits at No. 7 on ESPN's pound-for-pound chart as he prepares to face undefeated Russian fighter Movsar Evloev, a bout that will be Volkanovski's 33rd professional fight, 12th UFC title fight and 19th in the promotion overall.

"Wow, there you go. It's crazy," Volkanovski said when those numbers were put to him. "It's crazy because even though I know I'm world champion -- or two-time world champion -- I know I was pound-for-pound No. 1, I know I've broken records, but it's weird, it doesn't feel like I've done that much in the UFC. It's hard to explain. It's like, at the end of the day, I do know that I've done it, but I don't live my life thinking I've done that. Does that make sense? It's not even close to a thought of mine.

"I guess it's just because I'm always myself and I just forget about the fighting thing. And I come into the gym and then I've got a job to do and that's that. But then I go back home and then I sort of forget about it all. I don't know why it is that way."

It's that mentality that has endeared Volkanovski to not just Australia, but to fight fans the world over. Just a few weeks on from his 38th birthday, the two-time UFC champion remains as popular as ever.

But having completed another lap around the sun, the questions about his ability to continue compete in arguably the most brutal sport on the earth grow louder than ever.

They just seem to wash right over Volkanovski, however.

"A lot of people will be like, 'F--- this, I'm over this, man. I've had enough.' But I'm still driven," Volkanovski said. "I feel like because I'm driven for these other little things -- other paths to success that still excite me because, I guess, they're different challenges. I'm always trying to challenge myself ... I love the fact that I'm 38 years old. I love the fact that he's [Evloev] undefeated. You name it. I love all these things."

Life outside the Octagon is also vastly different from when Volkanovski first stepped inside the cage.

Now a global sporting star, he has a hugely successful YouTube channel, which includes his "Cooking with Volk" series. He has his own clothing label, and just before flying out to Abu Dhabi for UFC 333, he attended the premiere of the new "Street Fighter" film, in which he plays the role of Joe.

Add to that a small hobby farm that keeps him busy -- he told ESPN that water issues have been plaguing his small cattle herd -- and four young daughters who keep him and wife, Emma, running in all directions.

Retirement no longer scares him. But that doesn't mean he's ready to roll over and accept that his UFC career is done. Volkanovski truly believes he is fighting as well as ever and is fully prepared for whatever Evloev throws at him.

"To fight an undefeated guy, 20-0, never lost in the UFC ... it's cool for [my] legacy. I love it," Volkanovski said.

"I'm going to show him that you know how to win against them other guys, just not me. And that's what I can't wait to go out there and prove. ... A lot of people are like, 'Oh, you know, he's a wrestler' ... but you're not just going to be able to lay on me or hold me down. So that's why now the old dog gets to take out this young guy. You're not hearing people really complain about it. People are excited for this fight, which is pretty cool. I don't need to try and sell it."

With a win in Abu Dhabi, Volkanovski would move to nine featherweight title wins, one clear of José Aldo, though he will have only tied the Brazilian for successful title defences with eight.

There is enough fresh blood at the top of the division to keep Volkanovski busy into 2027, though he has also suggested the idea of a "superfight" for the lightweight title with Justin Gaethje, saying: "Gaethje, Volk. I think he's said that he maybe has one more. That could be a superfight. Let's do a superfight with the lightweight title on the line. We can both see everyone off with a crazy superfight. That could be really good."

However, there is potentially a world in which Volkanovski continues to thwart the best the featherweight division has to offer.

And taking on a title fight beyond his 40th birthday, while unlikely, isn't totally out of the question.

"I can guarantee it won't be 40," Volkanovski said. "I mean, I say that now. It's like, '40, what?' And it's like, 'Mate, it's only two years away.'

"If you ask me that question differently, I'd be like, 'Could you see yourself in two years where I'm like, yeah, yeah, for sure.' But when you say 40, I'm like, 'Nah, I'm not doing 40.' But then here I am at 38. That's two years away. So it could definitely happen, right? But I mean, at the end of the day, none of that will matter. It's going to be how I'm handling things, what damage am I taking?"

What Volkanovski is certain of is that he will deliver a performance against Evloev to rival any from his esteemed UFC career, one that leaves the MMA world in no doubt as to whether he still has what it takes to fight on -- whether he chooses to or not.

"I've said this quite a few times now, that this may be a fight where all you guys are going to be saying that this is probably the best Volk we've ever seen," he told ESPN.

"Do I still believe I'm better than all of them? 100%. But not just that, the fight that this fight's going to bring, and the fight that I'm going to bring, stylistically, you guys will come out of this [saying] that's one of Volk's best performances.

"How, at 38, is Alex pulling off his best f---ing performance? I believe that's what you are going to be saying after this."

stories.headline: Consensus top AFL draft prospect Dougie Cochrane already in rare air
stories.summary: Missing significant chunks of football hasn't stopped Port Adelaide NGA star Dougie Cochrane from firming as the top prospect in this year's AFL draft.
stories.body:
It's rare for a player to be the consensus no. 1 rated prospect in their draft. From coaches to recruiters and a myriad of draft evaluators, Dougie Cochrane stands atop 2026's crop. For him to do so after playing just four games in his top-age campaign puts the Port Adelaide NGA gun in rare air.

The starring junior missed both years of his u18 national championships through injury, and this year only returned to the field in the final month of the season. But what he produced at league level last season and amongst his peers at the u16s national championships in 2024 is not easily forgotten.

Clearly a class above at the national championships three years ago, Cochrane put all of his skill and athleticism on show. He was a distributor out of defence, won aerial duels around the ground and was the focal point of the SA forward line in a showing of his unique versatility.

From there he made his league debut for Central Districts as a 17-year-old, kicking four goals including an outrageous snap on his left foot from the pocket after crumbing a forward 50 contest. From his first game he was already the best player on the ground.

Speaking to ESPN ahead of the draft combine Cochrane was a bit flat. It wasn't because he'd missed his top-age season, he knew he wasn't going to be testing, and he knew most clubs wouldn't bother booking an interview given his ties to Port Adelaide. But there was one thing that really got to him.

"They measured me at 194-and-a-half centimetres," he tells ESPN with a grin. "They took a centimetre off me, but we'll round that up."

At six-foot-four (we'll round it up too) he's widely considered the next elite key forward prospect to come through the AFL Draft. Only he doesn't necessarily see it that way.

"I want to be a midfielder when I'm older, that's what I'm striving towards. "For right now I'm pretty happy forward, if not back. I'm happy wherever the team needs, whatever the team needs.

"I'm pretty skinny right now, I'm not as muscly as the Patty Cripps's of the world, the Bonts of the world. I want to focus on my midfield craft and get that experience."

Cochrane missed a significant chunk of his bottom-age year with a hamstring and over the off-season underwent knee surgery to address patella tendinitis. He didn't play for 11 straight months from the end of 2025 to July 2026.

Watching from the sidelines frustrated him but he knew it was all out of an abundance of caution.

"I started playing league at Centrals last year, I sort of started feeling [knee pain] a little bit. I thought nothing of it, just thought it was a bit of growing pain. It got worse and worse by the time I started doing pre-season... when you take off and do your powerful stuff it flares up.

"They did a clean out of it... I had the surgery, and I walked out of the surgery. It was two little key holes."

Cochrane sat down with ESPN as Port Adelaide list manager Jason Cripps all but confirmed on Trade Radio Essendon would be bidding on the gun academy prospect at pick one in the 2026 AFL Draft.

He's the son of Port Adelaide and North Melbourne midfielder Stuart Cochrane, and grew up supporting the Power after his dad's playing career finished up. His brother Tom was on the list during formative years and the club is set up to match his bid wherever it lands.

"Dad's been my idol growing up. Looking up to him, I obviously didn't get to see him play but he's been enormous."

Asked if it would mean more being that first selection on November 19, Cochrane's humble nature shines through.

"I loved watching the draft growing up, seeing those high picks. The pick doesn't really matter, does it? There have been a lot of picks over times where the number one picks haven't gone as well as they should've. I just want to end up at an AFL club - wherever that is I don't mind - but I just want to play footy," he says.

"Growing up and supporting Port all my life, it would be special playing for them. But whatever happens happens and I'm just gonna let that decide itself."

stories.headline: NRL transfer whispers: Bulldogs closing in on Skelton return; Panthers lock in Patea
stories.summary: The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1. Isaac Issa has news from the Dragons on some key outside backs
stories.body:
The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1, with clubs beginning to shape their rosters for 2027 and beyond.

From player movement to changes behind the scenes, ESPN NRL Insider Isaac Issa has the latest whispers from around the competition.

Cowboys open to keeping Taumalolo

North Queensland are open to retaining Jason Taumalolo beyond 2027, with the veteran forward's assessment of how his body is holding up set to guide the next step.

ESPN understands the Cowboys will take their lead from Taumalolo as he weighs up his playing future, reflecting his standing as a club legend.

Taumalolo is contracted until the end of next season and becomes eligible to negotiate with rival clubs for 2028 onwards from November 1.

Panthers lock in Patea
Penrith have secured Tua Patea until the end of 2029, with the youngster signing an extension that includes a pathway from a development contract into the club's top 30.

Patea capped off the 2026 season with a hat-trick in the Panthers' Jersey Flegg Grand Final victory, having started the year with an NRL training block.

The new deal will see him join Penrith's full-time NRL squad as he works towards a first-grade debut.

Bulldogs closing in on Skelton return

Jeral Skelton is closing in on a return to Canterbury following his departure from the Wests Tigers.

ESPN understands the Bulldogs are in advanced discussions to bring the outside back to the club for the 2027 season.

An agreement is understood to be close, although the deal has yet to be finalised.

Multiple NRL sides eye Knights forward

A Sydney club and a Queensland-based club are monitoring Newcastle forward Mat Croker ahead of November 1.

ESPN understands the two clubs have shown interest in the 27-year-old, who is approaching the final year of his Knights contract and can negotiate with rivals for 2028 onwards from next month.

Rivals keeping tabs on Dragons' Tu

Multiple clubs are monitoring St George Illawarra outside back Setu Tu, with the Dragons yet to begin talks over a contract extension.

Tu is contracted until the end of 2027 and is expected to test the open market from November 1, when rival clubs can negotiate a deal for 2028 and beyond.

The former Warriors outside back joined the Dragons on a development contract this season and is set to move into the club's top 30 squad in 2027.

His ability to cover multiple positions across the backline adds to his appeal as clubs assess their recruitment options.

Rivals monitor Patea as open market looms
Penrith young gun Luron Patea is expected to test the open market from November 1, with multiple clubs keeping tabs on the promising prop.

Patea is contracted until the end of 2027, but the Panthers are yet to begin talks over an extension, leaving rival clubs poised to explore a deal for 2028 and beyond.

Penrith have not granted Patea permission to negotiate with other clubs before November 1.

The Panthers junior made his NRL debut in 2024 and has shown promise during his first-grade opportunities, providing another emerging option in Penrith's forward pack.

He is among several Panthers players approaching the final year of their contracts, with veteran prop Moses Leota also unsigned beyond 2027.

Roosters eye Dockar-Clay reunion
The Roosters have shown interest in a potential return for Zach Dockar-Clay as they explore options to bolster their hooking and utility depth.

ESPN understands the 31-year-old has emerged as an option following his departure from Manly, with discussions remaining at an early stage.

Dockar-Clay spent the 2024 and 2025 seasons with the Roosters before joining the Sea Eagles on a one-year deal for 2026.

Manly confirmed his departure last month after a season in which he claimed the club's NSW Cup best-and-fairest award.

Bostock brushes Dragons links

Dolphins star Jack Bostock has dismissed recent links between himself and the Dragons, admitting this isn't the first time he'd been floated for a club switch.

"I've been linked to a few a clubs," Bostock admitted.

"I don't know about [the Dragons links]."

He said that while he "obviously sees it in the media," his sole focus is the Kangaroos.

Sloan's Dragons stay still a possibility

Tyrell Sloan could yet remain at St George Illawarra next season, with discussions ongoing over a potential stay despite his planned move to Castleford.

There is interest in keeping Sloan at the Dragons, but several hurdles remain before that can become a reality.

Roster space and salary cap room would need to be worked through, while any arrangement would also require Castleford to agree to release him.

Sloan previously admitted he would "love to" remain in the NRL when speaking to Channel Nine in August, after his Castleford deal had been announced.

No agreement has been reached and a stay is far from guaranteed.

stories.headline: Who are Como? The vacation-destination club that just rocked Man United
stories.summary: Seven years ago, Como were a team of amateurs. Now they're a Champions League club with a brand born from the city's reputation as a holiday hotspot.
stories.body:
COMO, Italy -- Como don't have a rich history of success. They don't have a full trophy cabinet or a state-of-the-art stadium. They don't have superstar players. Instead, they're making the most of what they do have to stand out from the pack: a lake, a picture-postcard location and a playground for the rich and famous.

Where other football clubs have been apprehensive about chasing tourists for fear of alienating local supporters, Como are cashing in. With their 12,000-capacity Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia just a few steps away from Lake Como and Hollywood royalty among those regularly jetting in and out, the club proudly market themselves as a "sports tourism destination."

The aim has been to build a team, but also a sustainable business around it. And it's working.

The change of direction off the pitch under Indonesian owners Djarum Group has coincided with spectacular success on it. Declared bankrupt twice since 2003, Como were playing in Italy's amateur fourth tier as recently as 2018-19. But after three promotions in six years, in 2024 they ended a 21-year wait to return to Serie A.

Manager Cesc Fàbregas orchestrated a fourth-place finish last season, enough to qualify for the UEFA Champions League for the first time in their 119-year history, and on Wednesday night, they welcomed Manchester United to their idyllic home nestled in the hills of Lombardy.

"It's definitely something that I was not expecting to see in my life," Elena Roda, a Como fan for more than 40 years, tells ESPN. "I still cannot really understand how we actually managed to get to the Champions League. It's definitely something that I was not expecting. I'm living this like a dream."

On Wednesday afternoon, the shopping trips and quiet coffees in Como's squares were interrupted by United fans breaking out into loud chants about former striker Andy Cole. Where there had been tourists holding maps and guidebooks around the southern tip of the lake on Tuesday, 24 hours later they had been replaced with football fans draped in Como blue streaming toward the stadium.

By Wednesday night, after braving lashing winds and pouring rain, it was the supporters dressed in blue, locals and tourists alike, who went home happy. On the most glamorous night in the club's history, rising star No. 10 Nico Paz channeled the electricity in the storm clouds above and Como celebrated a superb 4-1 win over Man United.

Como's remarkable rise began with an experiment that never got off the ground.

Taken over by Djarum Group in 2019, the initial idea was to fill the team with Indonesian youth players and broadcast the games at home.

"I was working for a television station and we just lost the rights to the Italian League," Como president Mirwan Suwarso tells ESPN. "At the time we had a project, a program, where Indonesian boys, national team players, were training in Birmingham and playing against academy teams in England.

"The ratings were comparable to that of the Premier League. So we thought it was a great idea to buy an Italian club and put the players in there."

But an unexpected promotion killed the idea and forced the owners into a rethink.

"Little did I know that three months after we bought it, the team got promoted into the third division, became professional, and you're no longer allowed to have foreign players," Suwarso said. "So the idea became obsolete. We had to pivot and we changed it into a documentary series. You can still find it on YouTube. Then when we got promoted into the second division, the costs became so high.

"We couldn't sustain it. We struggled. At that point in time, my owner said: 'We've got to turn this around into a business. Either we sell and find a buyer today to recoup our money or develop this into a business that becomes profitable for us and beneficial for the group.'

"There were offers coming in and the offers were good. It convinced them to say: 'Wait, if people are wanting to buy this, maybe there is a real business behind it.'"

That's where the lake comes in.

It's estimated that tourism at Lake Como brings in around €1.5 billion every year. Some locals trace the boom back to George Clooney buying a house on the lake in 2002. Robert Pattinson and Sylvester Stallone also own property in the small towns along the waterfront.

"The business here is not about just the football team," Suwarso says. "We're not strong enough to be that, but we should be a place where people want to come to have a good time and watch football while they're here.

"That's the beauty of it, because we are so small with only 83,000 people in the city. We knew the growth had to come from overseas."

A hotspot for holidays, Como have embraced football fans from all over the world keen to watch a game as part of their trip.

"It's quite strange being a local fan to see all these people coming to Como to the games and also buying a lot of jerseys and merchandising," Roda says. "We were not used to that, but we know that also that we have to embrace it. I think that it's something normal when a team becomes important. It's strange but we are getting accustomed to it."

The Isle of Wight fan chapter began when a group of friends visiting Milan realized neither of the city's two teams -- AC Milan and Inter Milan -- were playing, and instead made the 25-mile trip to watch Como. The Como Tartan Army in Scotland has 3,000 members.

"When we came here in 2019 before COVID, [the region had] maybe 1.9 million tourists," said Suwarso. "Last year, we had 5.6 million tourists. I wish I could say it was down to us, but there's a few big people that did things here like George Lucas making Star Wars, George Clooney having a house, and Logan Paul getting engaged here. Barack Obama has holidayed here, and Michael Jordan.

"They have elevated the allure of this place so much and we benefit from it."

Hugh Grant, Andrew Garfield, Kate Beckinsale, Keira Knightley, Michael Fassbender, Adrien Brody, Benedict Cumberbatch and Terry Crews all have attended games. For those seeking a luxury tourism experience, the team operates a private members' club called The Club On The Lake. Located in an 18th-century villa a short walk from the stadium, it includes a rooftop lounge, Michelin-starred restaurant, library, music lounge and games room. Membership costs around €4,500 a year.

The Como Cup was created so there are games in July and August, when tourism is at its peak. Crystal Palace, Lens and Villarreal were among the teams competing last summer.

Attracting tourists comes with its own pressure, though. Visitors want to sample a football match in one of Europe's top leagues, but they also want to be entertained.

"If we are benefiting from the number of people that come here, we would love them to come to the stadium as well and watch a football match," Suwarso said. "But if the football is crap, why would they come and watch it? So we have to play attractive football.

"Lake Como is about serenity, tranquillity, but it's about beauty. So the football has to be attractive and beautiful. That's what Cesc Fàbregas has built for us."

If the setting is key to Como's brand, then Fàbregas -- head coach since November 2023 -- is the central figure when it comes to the football side. The Spaniard initially joined as a player in 2022 when the club were in Serie B before coaching the club's under-19s and B teams.

"We sat down one day with Mirwan and he asked me what was my plan, what was my vision," remembers Fàbregas, who describes the starting point for Como's growth as "not just zero, but minus-10."

"I presented the whole thing about what we could achieve together and we put a plan to work. We tried to bring young players that nobody knew that much, we believed in them and they responded really well.

"Mirwan is taking care of things off the pitch and then he gave me the keys to the football zone. We work together as a team and trust each other. That's the most important thing."

Historically, Italian football is defensive and attritional. Fàbregas, though, was educated at Barcelona, where style is everything. His ideas fit well in a city that oozes class and sophistication.

"When Cesc started coaching our youth team, I saw that the football was different," Suwarso said. "I watched one game, I think it was Como against Inter's youth team, and Cesc had a team with no defenders because we didn't have a youth team two years before that. And yet we were beating Inter in a way that's so attractive to watch.

"It convinced me to put him in charge of the first team earlier rather than later. ... We wanted to have a blueprint that he's created, the idea of the way we want to play. Football the Como way."

It's football that has elevated Fàbregas' stock as a head coach and taken Como all the way to the Champions League. Now here, the club are using the opportunity to attract more new fans while also rewarding the ones who have been there from the start.

Ahead of their first league phase game against RB Leipzig -- a 4-1 win -- a number of directors gave up their tickets to allow some of the club's oldest supporters to attend.

For Manchester United's visit, a group of Como's most loyal fans who have followed the team through the divisions were invited onto the pitch to wave the Champions League banner before kickoff. It's a nod to the core fanbase at a time when Como are also utilizing their unique selling points to grow beyond the city they call home.

"Everyone buys into it," says Fàbregas. "Sometimes fans have one idea, directors have another idea, staff have another idea and the city has another idea. We are the total package.

"I think this is very special and we need to continue like this. If we keep working hard, I think the story of Como will be very beautiful."

Max Verstappen claimed his second victory this season after winning the Singapore Grand Prix for the first time.

Kimi Antonelli continued to extend his lead in the title championship to 102 points from Mercedes teammate George Russell, and there is a mathematical chance he will be able to clinch the title in Austin.

Circuit of the Americas

The Circuit of the Americas first hosted the United States Grand Prix in 2012, to mark the end of a five year wait since the race at Indianapolis.

Mario Andretti, who won the world championship in 1978, opened the track and it has become a popular race among drivers and fans alike with plenty of overtaking action and drama.

COTA is a varied circuit with straights, esses through to sector two, and a series of hair-pins in sector three. The high-speed corners takes some inspiration from Silverstone and Hockenheim.

It's a mix of fast corners, long straights and has one of the steepest elevation climbs to Turn 1.

Norris finished second and cut his lead to 14 points to Piastri in the standings, who finished fifth. Verstappen ended the weekend only 40 points behind Piastri with five races left of the season.

Who will win this year?

Antonelli will be as focused as ever to claim his ninth victory of the season with one hand already on the drivers' championship trophy.

However, Mercedes are still working on how to best optimise its current upgrade package. Last time out in Singapore, the team ran Russell on the older specification, while Antonelli had the upgraded package.

Red Bull were labelled by rivals as the "team to beat" for the remaining six races of the season. There seems to be no stopping Verstappen, who has won the U.S. Grand Prix four times.

Don't count out Hamilton who holds the record for six wins around COTA and will be looking to get his seventh podium for Ferrari this season.

stories.headline: Ruben Amorim with 'nothing to say' about Man United on return to England
stories.summary: Ruben Amorim insisted he had "nothing to say" about Manchester United ahead of AC Milan's Europa League clash at Bournemouth on Thursday night.
stories.body:
Ruben Amorim insisted he had "nothing to say" about Manchester United ahead of AC Milan's Europa League clash at Bournemouth on Thursday night.

The 41-year-old was sacked by United in January after 14 months in charge, and was appointed by the Serie A side in June.

Amorim revealed he does not think he has changed as a person since his time with the Red Devils, but believes he has become better at his job.

"Overall, I think the important thing is that I'm here as AC Milan's manager," said Amorim, speaking at a press conference at the Vitality Stadium and quoted by Milan News.

"I have nothing to say about United. I can say that I loved the club and the atmosphere: what happened doesn't change that.

"Then I moved on, now I'm at AC Milan and I'm focused on this: at every big club, problems are always around the corner. I focus on ourselves and I don't think about the teams. My past at United doesn't matter; what I said when I signed there remains the same."

Amorim revealed Samuel Chukwueze is out with a hip problem, and Gonçalo Ramos has sustained a calf strain, and expects 19-year-old Alphadjo Cissè, who he believes has reached only "50 per cent of his potential" to feature in Thursday's line-up to face the Cherries.

"I have more experience as a coach, but I'm not a different person," Amorim added, reflecting on his spell with United.

"I understand football better, and that will help me deal with problems in the future. I think I'm the same person, just a little more experienced in some things."

The man who replaced Amorim at United, Michael Carrick, has seen his position come under serious pressure in recent weeks as the club have endured a torrid start to the new season.

His team were beaten 4-1 by Cesc Fabregas' Como in Italy on Wednesday in a match that saw Carrick and Fernandes appear to trade barbs through their post-match comments to the travelling media.

stories.summary: St. Louis goalkeeper Roman Bürki was taken to the hospital after taking a knock to the head during the U.S. Open Cup final against the Columbus Crew.
stories.body:
St. Louis City goalkeeper Roman Bürki was taken to the hospital after taking a knock to the head in a collision during his team's U.S. Open Cup final win over the Columbus Crew on Wednesday night.

In an attempt to make a save in the 70th minute, Bürki took a knee to the head from Crew winger Anass Zaroury. He remained on the ground to receive medical attention before being stretchered off the field.

Bürki was able to wave to supporters as he was taken away from the pitch. St. Louis confirmed to ESPN that Bürki was conscious and moving all extremities on his way to the hospital.

The score was tied 0-0 at the time of the injury, but St. Louis went on to win the game in a shootout after Burki's backup Ben Lundt made a save to help his team beat the Crew 5-3 on spot kicks.

The win earned St. Louis, which began play in MLS in 2023, its first trophy in club history.

St. Louis City captain Bürki had 43 touches and three crucial saves before the injury. He played an integral role in maintaining the 0-0 draw before being replaced by Lundt after the head injury.

Bürki, who joined St. Louis from Borussia Dortmund in 2022, stopped a corner kick from Brais Méndez that appeared to be goalbound and a flurry of other shots just before sustaining his injury.

Eleven minutes of injury time was added due to Bürki's injury, but neither team scored before the end of regulation despite Columbus outshooting St. Louis 16-3, so the game went to extra time and penalties.

stories.headline: Senators fans booing Tkachuk reminiscent of previous unpleasant sports returns
stories.summary: Brady Tkachuk isn't the first notable sports figure to be met with jeers by fans of his prior team.
stories.body:
On Wednesday night, months of mixed emotions for Ottawa Senators fans came to a head as Brady Tkachuk made his first trip back to the Canadian Tire Centre as a member of the Florida Panthers.

The Senators drafted Tkachuk in 2018, and he made three All-Star teams with the franchise. After being swept in the first round by the Carolina Hurricanes this past season, however, Tkachuk asked to be traded from the team so he could join his brother Matthew Tkachuk in Florida.

Senators fans let him have it when he took the ice, showering him with boos.

Tkachuk isn't alone in hearing the boo-birds on coming back to his former club, but if we were to include every contentious homecoming in sports, this article would drag on longer than an awkward encounter with your ex. Instead, we'll just regale you with some of the most memorable ones.

Juan Soto in New York, 2025

Soto spent the 2024 season with the Yankees before landing a 15-year $765 million contract with the Mets in the 2024 offseason. What was Soto welcomed to as his first time to Yankee Stadium as a Met? A shower of boos.

On top of that, every time Soto took the field on defense, Yankee fans also turned their backs on the right fielder.

John Calipari in Lexington, 2025

Calipari spent a decade and a half leading the Kentucky Wildcats before trading blue for red and accepting the Arkansas Razorbacks job last spring. Kentucky went to the Final Four four times under Calipari -- capturing a national title in 2011-12 -- but finished in unceremonious fashion each of his past four seasons.

The reaction when Calipari walked onto the court in his return to Lexington? A chorus of boos.

James Harden in Philadelphia, 2023

Harden spent a season and a half with the Philadelphia 76ers before being traded to the LA Clippers in October 2023. He requested a trade during the 2023 offseason and later called 76ers president Daryl Morey a liar after not being traded initially.

Philadelphia fans welcomed him as only they could -- booing Harden heavily during introductions and every time he touched the ball. They also cheered during his missed shots.

LeBron James in Cleveland, 2010

James went from being hailed as a hero to jeered as a villain quicker than the writers of "Game of Thrones."

The environment was nothing short of combative as James returned to Cleveland for the first time as a member of the Miami Heat. The feelings of betrayal, disappointment and vitriol directed at him were tangible in the arena -- and in the city as a whole.

LeBron hadn't just been the most popular sports figure in Cleveland, he was one of its own. So his departure for South Beach brought about a different level of anguish to the championship-starved city that had its hopes and dreams resting upon his shoulders.

The "kid from Akron" was showered with boos and obscenities from former fans. Some of them threw things (including beverages and a battery); others held signs featuring things such as "Quitness" and "Witnessed No Championship," along with the more straightforward "I Hate LeBron." According to the team, four fans were ejected, and one was arrested that night.

King James powered through the animosity to score 38 points en route to a 118-90 Heat win.

LeBron would go on to regain Cleveland's love with a hard-earned Larry O'Brien Trophy in 2016.

Jack Eichel in Buffalo, 2022
Eichel, a Vegas Golden Knights forward and former Buffalo Sabres captain, was traded in November 2022. He had zero points in Vegas' 3-1 loss at the KeyBank Center in March 2022 while being showered with boos from his former supporters.

The return trip was a bit different, aside from the same raucous chorus of boos.

Eichel had a hat trick in the Golden Knights' 7-4 win over the Sabres. That extended Vegas' win streak to nine games. This time, Eichel seemed to relish playing the heel.

"I think last year I didn't know what to expect," Eichel said after the game. "I had an emotional connection -- I still do -- to this city and these people. I came in this year knowing what I was going to get and the kind of reception. I just tried to use the energy."

Bryce Harper in Washington, 2019

From favored son to public enemy No. 1, Harper, who left the Washington Nationals to sign a then-record-breaking 13-year, $330 million deal with their National League East rival Philadelphia Phillies in February 2019, didn't garner an exceptionally warm welcome when he returned to Nationals Park for the first time.

Fans showered him with boos during a pregame tribute video, then cheered loudly as ace Max Scherzer struck him out in his first at-bat. The heckling didn't sit well with Harper as he called fans out after the game, saying they "crossed the line."

Some will argue this reception was petty as Harper simply went to the highest bidder; others will say loyalty should count for something.

We'll just say this: The Nationals went on to win the World Series the season after he left.

Kevin Durant in Oklahoma City, 2017

Golden State Warriors vs. Oklahoma City Thunder: A game to live in NBA infamy. No departure had caused such a ruckus around the Association since King James was hounded for "The Decision."

You didn't have to spend much time in OKC to see just how much Kevin Durant meant to the city -- the guy even had a restaurant named after him (the establishment closed in the wake of his departure but has since reopened with a different name and theme).

Subsequently, the welcome KD received was far from friendly. There were deafening boos while he warmed up, when he was introduced and whenever he touched the ball on offense. There were also cupcake signs -- so many cupcake signs. Not to mention at least one fan dressed as an actual cupcake.

To make matters worse, there was the messy divorce from his former teammate and friend, Russell Westbrook, which added a whole other layer of animosity. Things got chippy between the ex-duo throughout the game, and they exchanged words on several occasions. At one point during the contest, Westbrook could be seen yelling: "I'm coming!"

Durant got the last laugh, though, dropping 34 points and grabbing nine rebounds as the Warriors secured a dominant 130-114 victory. After the game, he commented on the persistent boos, saying: "I actually thought it would be a little louder, but it was fun."

Deion Sanders in Atlanta, 1994

Sanders, who played for the Atlanta Falcons for five years, left the city outraged after signing with the San Francisco 49ers. There was more ill will in the wake of his departure, as Falcons players claimed he demanded preferential treatment. They also said "Prime Time" really meant "Part Time" because Sanders split time between the Atlanta Braves and the Falcons.

This heated homecoming tale was a bit dissimilar to the others: Rather than enduring the relentless ridicule during his return to the Georgia Dome, Sanders taunted the Falcons faithful.

That's right, Prime Time flipped the script. He put on a show. It wasn't enough to high-step the final 40 yards into the end zone on a 93-yard interception return, he decided to turn sideways and flash a big ole grin toward the Atlanta bench for good measure.

The more they booed, the more he thrived (and danced).

The 49ers would go on to win 42-3.

Johnny Damon in Boston, 2006

All's fair in love and baseball -- except for leaving the Boston Red Sox for the New York Yankees. You really just can't do it. We mean, you can, but you're going to get publicly reprimanded for it.

One of the most heated rivalries in sports is not something to be trifled with, just ask Damon. The former Boston star was granted some leniency because of his involvement in bringing the Sox a World Series title, but the fans were still pretty brutal in his return to Fenway Park.

Many of them opted to throw fake and real dollar bills on the warning track in center when he took the field as an ode to his departure -- he left to sign a four-year contract with New York that was worth $12 million more than what Boston offered.

Damon drew extra criticism for joining the Yankees in December 2005 after vowing earlier in the year that "there's no way I can go play for the Yankees, but I know they're going to come after me hard. It's definitely not the most important thing to go out there for the top dollar, which the Yankees are going to offer me. It's not what I need."

Jaromir Jagr in Pittsburgh, 2001

Jagr won two Stanley Cups as a member of the Pittsburgh Penguins, but he didn't see a viable future as a Penguin, which left a bitter taste in the mouths of many Pens fans. More than that, it was the way in which he departed from the franchise (asking to be traded twice) that prompted the barrage of boos whenever he touched the puck while visiting Mellon Arena.

During the 2000-01 season, Jagr was going through a bit of a slump. That, combined with his rocky relationship with then-head coach Ivan Hlinka, the return of Mario Lemieux from retirement and the Penguins' inability to pay Jagr the big bucks, would probably have been enough cause for both parties to move on. But before being traded to the Washington Capitals in 2001, he famously declared, "I feel like I'm dying alive. ... I don't feel comfortable here right now. It's not the same for me right now. We'll see what happens. Maybe I'm going to think about retirement pretty soon."

While his threat to retire at the age of 28 was idle, it didn't bode well for his relationship with the Penguins organization or its fan base.

Alex Rodriguez in Seattle, 2001

Is it always about money in baseball? That was a rhetorical question.

Similar to the stories of Harper and Damon, Rodriguez's departure from Seattle had to do with a payday. Rodriguez, widely considered to be the best player in the game at the time, jilted the Seattle Mariners in favor of a 10-year, $252 million contract with the Texas Rangers during the offseason. At the time, it was the most lucrative contract in sports history.

The fans did not hesitate to voice their displeasure as Rodriguez came up for his first at-bat as a Ranger. The boos at Safeco Field were deafening -- and persistent.

The game ended in a 9-7 Mariners victory.

Vince Carter in Toronto, 2005

Carter's relationship with Toronto has been a complicated one over the years. On Dec. 17, 2004, the former Raptors phenom was traded to the New Jersey Nets amid reports that he was displeased with Toronto's upper management. Rumors also circulated that he had stopped giving his all on the court.

It's no surprise that the thought of Vinsanity quitting on the team did not go over well with the Raptors' faithful. The underwhelming return from the trade of Alonzo Mourning (who refused to report and was released immediately), Aaron Williams, Eric Williams and two first-round draft picks only added insult to injury.

When Carter made his return to Toronto donning a New Jersey uniform on April 15, 2005, the sold-out crowd let him hear it with a steady stream of boos and "V.C. sucks" chants.

Carter remained unfazed and went on to score 39 points as the Nets left town with a 101-90 victory. He would make a habit of putting on impressive performances in The Six for years to come.

Eric Lindros in Philadelphia, 2002

Lindros played eight seasons with the Philadelphia Flyers before things unraveled. On May 26, 2000, in Game 7 of the Eastern Conference finals, an open-ice hit left him with the sixth concussion of his career. Lindros was cleared to resume playing on Nov. 27, 2000, but he sat out the remainder of the season and vowed never to play for the Flyers again.

Lindros was traded to the New York Rangers. Despite insisting that his qualms in Philadelphia had solely been with the owner and general manager, Flyers fans didn't take kindly to his actions and made sure he was well aware when he returned to their home ice.

Terrell Owens in Philadelphia, 2006

Owens was embraced during his time with the Philadelphia Eagles, but as soon as he signed with the Dallas Cowboys, the love quickly turned to loathing. Fans united in common hatred for their former star, who had joined an NFC East rival.

Owens, who notoriously feuded with Philadelphia quarterback Donovan McNabb and criticized the Eagles before they released him and Dallas picked him, received an ice-cold homecoming to Lincoln Financial Field. Though McNabb maintained that he was immune to the T.O. hoopla surrounding the highly anticipated matchup, the city of Philadelphia was assuredly not.

The fans had emotionally invested in T.O, and thus they turned on him even harder. Owens joked in the week leading up to the game that the crowd was capable of throwing "cheesesteaks, batteries, Huggies, anything" at him.

However, it never really came to that as T.O. never had a chance to gloat. The former Eagle was held to three catches for 45 yards in Philadelphia's 38-24 win.

Ben Simmons in Philadelphia, 2022

Simmons was acquired from the 76ers in February of 2022 but was still in street clothes when the Nets traveled to Philadelphia in March, only facing his old team in late November.

While Simmons signed autographs for fans in the stands and played well early on -- putting up 11 points, 11 assists, 7 rebounds, 3 steals and 3 blocks -- the crowd was profane and merciless, booing him constantly as the Nets fell to the Joel Embiid- and James Harden-less 76ers 115-106.

stories.headline: Way-too-early AFL tiers: There's a clear flag favourite; 'silly season' winners and losers
stories.summary: Who are the 2027 flag favourites? Who are the legitimate contenders? And who should already be booking September holidays? It's our way-too-early edition of AFL tiers.
stories.body:
The 2026 AFL season is done and dusted, but that hasn't stopped ESPN's senior writer Jake Michaels from turning his attention to next year. Who are the 2027 flag favourites? Who are the legitimate contenders? And who should already be booking September holidays? It's our way-too-early edition of AFL tiers!

All of our best footy content, now on Instagram. Follow @espnfooty here!

Your new premiership favourite

1. HAWTHORN

Who knows if the Hawks would have been premiers this year if not for Hugh McCluggage's heroics late in that dramatic preliminary final at the MCG. There's certainly a real argument they would have gone all the way. This side, which is expertly coached by Sam Mitchell, just added Zach Merrett and Ben King to its best 23, two more experienced players desperate for flag success. There won't be many games the Hawks don't start favourite in next year. Even if this club's 2027 season over/under was set at preliminary final weekend, I'd still be taking the over.

Should be great, but there are some questions

2. BRISBANE

3. FREMANTLE

4. SYDNEY

The Lions just completed a remarkable three-peat and it certainly wouldn't have been outrageous for them to hold top spot here. But losing Lachie Neale and Chris Fagan -- arguably the two most important pieces of the club's modern-day dynasty -- cannot be underestimated. How do they fill those seismic gaps? The Dockers were the dominant team of the home and away season and if we played out the last four minutes of the Grand Final 100 times they probably win 99 of them. Instead, Fremantle has to spend all offseason dwelling on the greatest missed opportunity in club history. How do they respond in 2027? As for the Swans, who are always somewhere around the mark, nobody can really be sure what to expect after the Pullman Hotel saga. So many fascinating questions.

Silly season winners

5. GEELONG

6. WESTERN BULLDOGS

7. CARLTON

8. COLLINGWOOD

Each of these teams will be counting down the days until the 2027 season after drastically improving their lists during the trade and free agency window. The Cats landed the dynamic Toby Greene, significantly upgraded their ruck department with the singing of Rowan Marshall, and bolstered their defensive stocks with Jordan Ridley. The Bulldogs scored the biggest prize of all in Zak Butters, but they were also able to pry away Jordon Butts from the Crows, a much needed acquisition to what's been a shaky defence. The Blues will go into next season with Joel Amartey, Lachie Whitfield, and almost certainly father-son talent Cody Walker, while the Magpies added dual Brownlow medallist Lachie Neale and 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan.

Silly season losers

9. MELBOURNE

10. ADELAIDE

While a bunch of teams we'd expect to be in the fifth-to-10th range clearly improved their best 23, the Demons and Crows did nothing of the sort. Adelaide literally brought in nobody and will have to deal with the loss of key defender Jordon Butts, who departed as a free agent for the Bulldogs. Melbourne did sign several names, but do we think any of Zane Duursma, Will McLachlan, and Bodie Ryan can be needle movers in 2027? But hey, these were two sides I was down on this year and both ultimately outperformed expectations. Perhaps they do have it all figured out...

It's now or never

11. GOLD COAST

12. NORTH MELBOURNE

13. ST KILDA

If not now, then when? The Suns rocketed to co-flag favouritism this time last year after signing Christian Petracca and Jamarra Ugle-Hagan. They ultimately won just nine games and finished 13th on the ladder. Disastrous. Damien Hardwick is under serious pressure to get more out of this list. Meanwhile, the Kangaroos haven't played finals in a decade, but there's some newfound optimism after the senior coaching appointment of highly regarded Jaymie Graham and the signing of Nick Blakey, the biggest name the club has attracted in a decade. The Saints also need to show something early in 2027 or Ross Lyon could be on his way out ... again! But the real worry is not doing enough to ensure star midfielder Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera signs on.

It's going to be another long year

14. PORT ADELAIDE

15. GWS

16. WEST COAST

17. RICHMOND

18. ESSENDON

Perhaps I'm being a tad harsh on Port, who were pretty competitive this year. But at the end of the day we're taking Zak Butters out of a side that won just seven games. The Giants lost four of their best players in Toby Greene, Jesse Hogan, Lachie Whitfield, and Kieren Briggs, and will be relying heavily on their younger talent next year. And then there's the Eagles, Tigers, and Bombers -- three teams that combined for just nine wins this year. We all expect these sides to be somewhere around the bottom of the ladder.
